original_pinned_run.note: The first retrieval reused the .env-pinned APIFY_RUN_ID, which was a single already-completed Apify actor run limited to 10 posts (limitPerSource=10, query='UnitedHealthcare RFA', datePosted=past-24h, deepScrape=true, cost $4.98). Only 1 of those 10 posts was classified S; 9 were Irrelevant generic content.
original_pinned_run.superseded_reason: User explicitly asked to fetch the real latest 100 LinkedIn activities. The pinned run could not be re-parameterized (it just re-reads a fixed completed run's dataset), so a new Apify run was launched instead, reusing the same actor/credentials already in .env.

current_retrieval.script_used: linkedin/fetch_linkedin_batch.py (new script, extends the existing Apify REST mechanism from fetch_linkedin.py/test_apify_connection.py by adding actor-run launch + poll, using the same actor and token already in this codebase)
current_retrieval.mechanism: POST https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/{actorId}/runs to launch a new run, poll GET .../actor-runs/{runId} until SUCCEEDED, then GET https://api.apify.com/v2/datasets/{datasetId}/items
current_retrieval.search_query: (UnitedHealthcare OR Aetna OR Cigna OR Humana OR Medicare) prior authorization denial reimbursement -- broadened from the original single-payer/single-procedure query to cover the multi-payer/multi-topic taxonomy already present in linkedin/process_linkedin.py. A more complex nested-boolean query with quoted procedure phrases (ESI, RFA, SCS, PNS, etc.) was tried first and rejected by LinkedIn's own search backend (confirmed via the run log: 'Unknown error when trying to fetch posts'); this flatter query is the confirmed-working version.
current_retrieval.shortfall_reason: LinkedIn's own search for this query genuinely only had 95 matching results at retrieval time within the actor's crawl -- not padded, not an error.
current_retrieval.cost_note: deepScrape was turned OFF (vs. the original pinned run's deepScrape=true) after a live test showed deepScrape drives ~$0.50/item in cost for comment-thread/reaction detail we don't need for classification; with it off, cost was negligible ($0.00005 total for 95 posts) while text/date/author/likes/comment-count/share-count are still included.
current_retrieval.classified_file: ../classified_rows_linkedin_100.json (used by consolidate.py in place of the old 10-item classified_rows_linkedin.json)
